Loo Finder · methodology

Useful because it is specific.

The Loo Finder is a curated London toilet directory built around a practical question: can you actually use the facility when you get there?

Coverage123 verified locations at launch
  • 01Public toilets
  • 02Transport hubs
  • 03Free cultural venues
  • 04Major shops and centres
01What is included

A smaller list with stronger evidence.

The database prioritises dedicated public toilets, TfL and rail facilities, free museums and galleries, major department stores, shopping centres and a small number of churches where toilet access is documented.

Ordinary pubs and cafés are deliberately excluded unless they participate in an official community toilet scheme. A large venue is not included simply because it probably has a toilet.

02How places are checked

Official evidence first.

Sources are ranked by reliability: councils and transport operators first, then venue operators and verified accessibility guides. Each record stores its source, verification date, coordinates and access attributes.

Where a store confirms toilets but does not explicitly promise access without purchase, the app says so. “Inside venue · no charge stated” is intentionally different from “Free confirmed”.

03Ranking

Distance matters most.

Results are primarily sorted by walking proximity. A modest penalty is applied to known paid facilities and less certain access, but the app will not hide a toilet next to you merely because a free one exists much farther away.

04Limits

Verified does not mean live.

Toilets can close temporarily, become unavailable for cleaning or maintenance, or change access policy. Opening hours are shown only where they can be represented with reasonable confidence. For time-sensitive decisions, the linked official source remains authoritative.

The principle

It is better to show fewer toilets with honest access information than thousands of pins that may waste your time.
